text: Abstract scan hypothesis: Port P cooperative mechanisms (cooperative objectives, memory, action recommendations) into Q double auction to test if they restore convergence to equilibrium. Rationale: Q shows LLM agents fail convergence; P shows cooperation+memory+recommendations enable coordination. Direct experimental test: modify Q agent architecture with P mechanisms, measure convergence rates vs Q baseline.

Q-P connexion analysis: Q double auction failure mode is strategic misalignment - agents cannot find equilibrium prices through bidding/asking behavior. P success mode is cooperative resource allocation under survival pressure. CRITICAL GAP: Double auctions are inherently competitive mechanisms; P cooperation mechanisms assume shared survival goal. Question: Can cooperation mechanisms designed for collective survival transfer to competitive price-discovery tasks? This is not a simple port - requires theoretical justification for why cooperative incentives would improve competitive market performance.

Mechanism mapping - what could transfer: (1) P memory system: agents track past outcomes to calibrate decisions. Q CoT shows agents struggle with price adjustment strategy - memory could help learn successful bidding patterns. (2) P action recommendations: agents suggest actions to peers. In Q context, this could enable price signal sharing or strategy hints. (3) P cooperative incentives: agents care about group survival. In Q, this conflicts with individual profit maximization inherent to double auctions. MOST PROMISING: Memory + recommendations without changing auction incentives. Test: Does information-sharing architecture improve convergence while keeping competitive payoffs?
